clue.text: Intellectual discovering bromine in breakfast food

indicators.note: in tells us the symbol for bromine is placed within the breakfast food

parts.note: cereal is a typical breakfast food
Br is the chemical symbol for bromine

explanation.surface: A thinker finds a chemical element in their morning cornflakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cerebral is brainy and given to thought, which is what an intellectual person is.

clue.text: Piece of armour stays around back of arsenal

indicators.note: around says the undergarment surrounds the other letter

parts.note: stays is an old word for a corset

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of the word arsenal

explanation.surface: Struts or guy ropes are set up around the rear of a weapons store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives L, the last letter of arsenal, which goes inside CORSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A corslet is a piece of body armour covering the trunk, so it is one piece of armour.

clue.text: Difficulty with stone not unknown

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the unknown out of the gemstone

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A problem with a gem whose origin is not mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: A rub is an obstacle or snag, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub', so it means a difficulty.

clue.text: Outlaw pleased he's worked the land

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
pleased means glad

indicators.note: worked means the letters of he's are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is happy to have farmed a field despite being banned from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges HES into ESH to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a country, a land; the definition is a little cryptic, as land suggests soil to till.

clue.text: Drinks spiked with old purgative drug

indicators.note: a drink spiked with something has it slipped inside, so the old letter goes into the drinks

parts.note: ales are drinks

explanation.surface: Beverages are laced with an aged laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloes is the bitter juice of the aloe plant, formerly used medicinally as a laxative or purge.

clue.text: German city with a long name

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A town in Germany bearing a lengthy title.
explanation.definitionFit: Aachen, also called Aix-la-Chapelle, is a city in western Germany.

clue.text: Top copy marked as incorrect?

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them
a cross, X, is the mark put by a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether the best duplicate was graded wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or summit of something, its top.

clue.text: Gold taken from historic setting for woman of Greece

indicators.note: setting for means the trimmed word surrounds the woman like a jewel's mount
taken from tells us to remove gold from the word historic

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Ellen is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Gold is stolen from an old-fashioned jewellery setting made for a Greek lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' leaves HISTIC once the gold is gone; 'setting for' then mounts the woman inside it, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenistic describes Greek culture and history, especially after Alexander, so it means of Greece.

clue.text: Stir in capital once demanding fresh exit from airport

parts.note: fresh means new
passengers leave the terminal for their plane through a gate

explanation.surface: Unrest in a former capital calls for a new way out of the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison: Newgate was a notorious London jail, closed in 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was the old London prison, and stir is slang for a jail, so it was a stir in the capital.

clue.text: Charming girl inducted by adept

indicators.note: to be inducted by is to be taken in, so the girl goes inside the word for adept

parts.note: adept means able, skilled
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A delightful young woman is initiated by an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, so it is a synonym of charming.

clue.text: Spirit shown by bird with brick

parts.note: the robin is a bird
a brick is an old-fashioned term for a reliable, kind person, a good fellow

explanation.surface: A ghost appears alongside a bird and a lump of masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: Brick in British slang means a dependable, generous person: 'you're a brick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous sprite of English folklore.

clue.text: Be like a vestal at the outskirts of Rome? That's dull

parts.note: a Vestal Virgin was sworn to chastity, so she would lack lust

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Life as a chaste priestess on the edge of Rome is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Vestal Virgins were Roman priestesses of Vesta bound to celibacy; the R and E of Rome finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre means lacking brilliance or vitality, hence dull.

clue.text: Scientist having lost first pair of stockings, Newton put off game

indicators.note: having lost says the scientist drops some letters

parts.note: a chemist is a scientist
the first two letters of stockings are S and T
N is the abbreviation for newton, the unit of force
to put off is to defer

explanation.surface: A researcher missing some hosiery and a famous physicist postpone their match.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a card game, a form of baccarat played in casinos.

clue.text: Divine consort from another age

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words another age

explanation.surface: A god's partner comes from a different era.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was the queen of the Greek gods and wife of Zeus, a goddess who was a consort.

clue.text: "Bird with Stick", penned by Rye's novelist

parts.note: a hen is a bird

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the stick goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Rye is a town in East Sussex; the possessive gives its letters plus S
to stick is to jam

explanation.surface: A story titled 'Bird with Stick' was written by a writer from Rye.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist lived at Lamb House in Rye, East Sussex, so the surface is apt; 'penned by' encloses the stick in the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist, author of The Portrait of a Lady.

clue.text: Altered dancing that requires footwork

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A changed dance routine that demands nimble feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever driving a machine, as on an old sewing machine, so it needs footwork.

clue.text: Entire cast extremely trendy hence destination of film?

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of trendy

explanation.surface: A whole film cast, all very fashionable, heads for a destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges ENTIRE to ETERNI; the film is From Here to Eternity.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title From Here to Eternity names a destination, so the question mark flags it.

clue.text: Hairstyle from which combs may be removed

definitions.meaning: a tall rounded hairdo popular in the 1960s

definitions.text: from which combs may be removed
definitions.meaning: honeycombs are taken from the hive a colony of bees builds

explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s bouffant is named after the domed hive of bees, which holds honeycombs.

clue.text: French artist not starting to impress university is under discussion

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the university goes inside
not starting means the artist's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Henri Matisse was a French painter

explanation.surface: A French painter who fails to make his mark on a college is the topic of debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops M from MATISSE, leaving ATISSE; U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: At issue is an idiom for the matter being debated, so it means under discussion.

clue.text: Reportedly, a means to control horse's charge

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the words are heard, not seen

parts.note: a rein is a means of controlling a horse

explanation.surface: A rider learns from hearsay how to steer a horse's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rein' said aloud sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally charge someone in court with an offence.

clue.text: Slip in rare broadcast by corporation

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of rare are thrown about

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A rare error occurs in a broadcast by a large company.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is a jocular British term for a big belly. 'broadcast' rearranges RARE to ERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, a slip.

clue.text: Rich, after change of direction, proceeded in leisurely fashion

indicators.note: change of direction means one compass point is swapped for another

parts.note: moneyed means rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy man, having turned round, strolled along.
explanation.definitionFit: To mosey is to amble or wander along unhurriedly.

clue.text: Free exhibition's opening as theme park attraction

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: Free admission to a show's launch at a theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride, such as a rollercoaster, is the main attraction at a theme park.

clue.text: Debating society with means of raising standards

parts.note: a Union is a university debating society, like the Oxford Union
jacks are devices for lifting heavy things such as cars

explanation.surface: A debating club discusses how to raise standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the Union Jack is the British flag.

clue.text: Headless rodent left for bird

indicators.note: headless means the rodent loses its first letter

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent without a head is left for a bird to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and related birds.

clue.text: Wounded in Indian Wars action, one is bent on submission

definitions.meaning: Wounded ___ was the 1890 massacre of Lakota people by US troops
a joint bent when kneeling in deference

explanation.definitionFit: The Wounded Knee massacre ended the Indian Wars; a person bends this joint to kneel in submission.

clue.text: Any limits in life at sea? Not a lot!

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor considers any boundaries to a life on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimally means to an immeasurably tiny degree, so it is barely anything.

clue.text: Settled for fine writing in condensed form

definitions.meaning: alighted, as a bird comes to rest

explanation.definitionFit: A bird that has landed has settled; lit is the abbreviation for literature.

clue.text: Disgruntled emperor's last appearance in nude

indicators.note: appearance in tells us the letter turns up inside the word for nude

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor is annoyed at his final appearance without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' gives R, from emperor, which goes inside NAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is British slang for annoyed or irritated, which is disgruntled.

clue.text: Shut up near unruly youth

parts.note: near means close
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s rebellious British youth

explanation.surface: A badly behaved teenager is locked in nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeted means shut away in a private room, so shut up.
